description: Four-role rhythm generator: each role has two voices but one set of outputs, carrying whichever fired last, with a three-band isolator, drive and a poly cable for Portal

params.text: Chooses the style that role's pattern is built from: W.African, Afro-Cuban, Brazilian, Balkan, Indian, Gamelan, Jazz, Electronic, Breakbeat or Techno
Sets how busy that role's pattern is, 0% to 90%
Sets how many steps that role's pattern runs for, 4 to 32
Shifts the pitch of that role's voices, one octave down fully anticlockwise to one octave up fully clockwise
Multiplies the decay of that role's voices, a fifth of the style's own length at the bottom of its travel to twice it at the top
Sets how far the patterns are allowed to drift from the straight style template each time round, 0% to 100%
Sets how far each hit is nudged off the grid in time and in level, 0% to 100%
Delays the off-beats, 0% for an even grid and 100% for the widest shuffle
Sets what share of the hits are dropped as rests, 0% to 100%
Sets how heavy a fill is when one is called for, 0% to 100%; at zero the fill jack does nothing
Shortens or lengthens the gates, 0% to 100%
Sets how far apart the four roles are placed in the stereo mix, all in the centre at 0% and at their full fixed spread at 100%
Builds a fresh set of patterns for every role from their current style, density and length settings
Returns every role to the start of its pattern
Crossfades that role between the drums built into the module and whatever is patched into its EXT IN jack, 0% for the synthesised drums and 100% for the patched signal
Cuts or lifts everything below 250Hz in the stereo mix: silence fully anticlockwise, unchanged in the middle, four times over fully clockwise
Cuts or lifts everything between 250Hz and 4000Hz in the stereo mix: silence fully anticlockwise, unchanged in the middle, four times over fully clockwise
Cuts or lifts everything above 4000Hz in the stereo mix: silence fully anticlockwise, unchanged in the middle, four times over fully clockwise

inputs.text: Each rising edge above 1V advances the patterns by one, two or four steps, according to the pulses-per-beat figure set on the menu
A rising edge above 1V returns every role to the start of its pattern
A rising edge above 1V builds a fresh set of patterns for every role
Added to the REST knob, ten points per volt
A rising edge above 1V rebuilds the patterns as a fill of the weight set by the FILL knob
Added to that role's STYLE knob, one style per volt
Added to that role's DENSITY knob, ten points per volt
Added to that role's FREQ knob, a fifth of an octave per volt
Added to that role's DECAY knob, 0.18 of the multiplier per volt
A signal for that role's first voice to play in place of its own drum, gated by that voice's envelope and scaled by its velocity

outputs.text: That role's audio, whichever of its two voices fired last, at the crossfade set by its MIX knob
A 10V gate for the length of that role's hit
That role's pitch as one volt per octave, with 0V standing for C4
That role's velocity as an envelope, 0V to 10V
The left side of the four roles panned apart by SPREAD, through the isolator and the drive, soft-clipped to ±5V
The right side of the four roles panned apart by SPREAD, through the isolator and the drive, soft-clipped to ±5V
All four roles on one sixteen-channel cable: four channels per role carrying audio, gate, pitch and velocity envelope in that order, ready for a Portal

notes: nothing steps until a clock reaches CLOCK. Patterns are built as soon as the module is placed, so REGEN is for changing them rather than for starting.
each role runs two voices but has one audio output, which carries whichever of the two struck most recently. There is no way to hear them separately.
the second external audio input of every role is declared but has no jack on the panel, so only the first voice of a role can be fed from outside.
menu: Clock PPQN — how many clock pulses make one beat: 1 PPQN (Quarter note), 2 PPQN (8th note) or 4 PPQN (16th note); the lower the figure, the more steps each clock advances
Random Exclusive — a submenu with a tick per role; a ticked role is left alone when the module is randomised
